title: Graphago: Accelerating SSD-based Graph Processing via Activity-Aware Graph Preprocessing
problem: SSD-based graph processing suffers from read amplification due to mismatch between large SSD access granularity (4KB) and small vertex data size; existing solutions are inefficient.
motivation: Out-of-core graph processing on SSDs is cost-effective but I/O bound; activity-aware optimization can improve throughput and reduce overhead.
method: Graphago preprocesses the graph before processing starts by predicting which vertices will be accessed frequently, then storing those vertices and their nearby neighbors close together on the SSD (activity-neighborhood ordering). It partitions the graph into chunks so frequently-accessed data is evenly distributed (active-data-balanced partitioning). This way, when the SSD reads a 4KB chunk to fetch one vertex, it brings along nearby vertices that the program actually needs, reducing wasted reads.
key_novelty: Activity-aware preprocessing—organizing the graph to place frequently-accessed vertices close together—reduces wasted disk reads and achieves a 4.8x speedup with reasonable preprocessing overhead.
contributions: Dual-centrality activity prediction model (local connectivity + global importance)
Activity-neighborhood graph ordering to minimize read amplification
Active-data-balanced partitioning for I/O load distribution
4.8x speedup vs. SOTA SSD-based systems with improved I/O efficiency
limitations: SSD-specific; activity prediction accuracy depends on workload; preprocessing overhead not negligible for small graphs; limited to graph traversal.
